title: Launch-day limits
scenario: A study-helper chat app launched on Monday. By noon there are three complaints: replies take 20 seconds to appear, some requests fail at peak hours, and long explanations stop mid-sentence. The team also hard-coded the context size in several files. You read the incident notes (exhibit).
exhibit:
incident notes, Monday

12:01  p95 time to full reply: 20s (UI shows spinner until done)
12:14  HTTP 429 x 340, header retry-after: 12
       app behaviour: retries instantly, 5 times
12:30  replies cut: stop_reason = max_tokens (cap: 300)
12:45  plan: move to vendor B; vendor B docs: 'rate limit is
       the larger of max_tokens and the estimated
       number of tokens'; proposal: set max_tokens = 100000
       on every call 'to be safe'

questions.prompt: Users stare at a spinner for 20 seconds. What change helps them most?

options.text: Stream the reply (stream: true) so text appears as it is generated.
options.explanation: Right. Streaming lets you show the beginning of the output while the model writes the rest. Handle errors that arrive mid-stream.

options.text: Raise max_tokens so the model finishes faster and the spinner ends sooner.
options.explanation: A higher cap allows longer replies; it does not make the first words appear sooner.

options.text: Move to the largest model available.
options.explanation: Larger models are often slower. The Claude comparison lists the largest models as slower.

options.text: Show nothing until the reply is complete, but add a progress bar and a cancel button.
options.explanation: That is the current design with decoration. Streaming shows real text early.

questions.prompt: How should the app handle the 429 errors?

options.text: Wait for the retry-after time, then retry with exponential backoff and jitter.
options.explanation: Right. Claude sends retry-after saying how long to wait; OpenAI recommends waiting longer after each failure, with random delay added, and honouring Retry-After.

options.text: Retry instantly five times, as it does now, until one call gets through.
options.explanation: Instant retries hit the same limit and add load. The header says to wait 12 seconds.

options.text: Treat 429 as a permanent failure and show an error message to the user right away.
options.explanation: A rate-limit 429 is temporary. Waiting and retrying usually succeeds.

options.text: Split each request into many tiny requests.
options.explanation: More requests use up the requests-per-minute limit faster.

questions.prompt: Replies stop with stop_reason max_tokens at a cap of 300. What is the right reading?

options.text: The cap is too low for these answers; raise it or continue the reply.
options.explanation: Right. max_tokens means the reply hit your limit, not that the model finished.

options.text: The context window is full, so the model had no room left to finish the answer.
options.explanation: A full context window gives a different signal (model_context_window_exceeded on Claude). This is your output cap.

options.text: The model refused to answer partway, so the reply ended early.
options.explanation: A refusal has its own stop_reason, refusal.

options.text: The rate limit cut the reply off once it passed 300 tokens.
options.explanation: Rate limits reject requests with 429; they do not end a reply with max_tokens.

questions.prompt: On vendor B, the team proposes max_tokens = 100000 on every call 'to be safe'. What is the problem?

options.text: A huge cap uses up vendor B's rate limit fast.
options.explanation: Right. Vendor B counts the larger of max_tokens and the estimated tokens toward the rate limit. That is OpenAI's documented rule. Claude's OTPM ignores max_tokens, so the same habit is cheap there but costly here. Set a cap that fits the task.

options.text: No problem. max_tokens never affects rate limits on any vendor.
options.explanation: The exhibit quotes vendor B saying the opposite. This differs by vendor.

options.text: The model will always write 100,000 tokens.
options.explanation: max_tokens is a ceiling, not a target. The issue is how vendor B counts it toward limits.

options.text: max_tokens must always equal the context window.
options.explanation: There is no such rule. The output cap should fit the expected answer.
